title: The Donkey and the Lion's Skin

keywords: the donkey and the lion's skin
full_text:
A foolish donkey, browsing through a hunter's yard, found the magnificent skin of a slain lion drying in the sun. A grand notion took root in his simple head: "If I dress myself in this royal coat, all the world will tremble before me, and I shall never have to haul heavy flour sacks again!"

He draped the lion's skin over his back, adjusting the great mane around his long ears and slipping his forelegs into the claws. Striding proudly into the village pastures, he assumed a fierce, lumbering posture.

The effect was instantaneous! The sheep scattered in blind panic, goats leaped over stone walls, cows stampeded into the brush, and the villagers fled into their cottages, barring doors and windows against the terrifying monster that stalked their lanes.

Puffed up with boundless vanity at his astonishing triumph, the donkey decided that a true King of the Forest must roar to establish his supreme dominion.

He threw back his head, opened his jaws wide, and attempted to unleash a terrifying, earth-shaking roar. But instead of a mighty feline bellow, out came a ridiculous, ear-splitting: "HEE-HAW! HEE-HAW-W-W!"

The villagers paused behind their shutters. The sheep stopped in their tracks. The village blacksmith burst out laughing, grabbed a heavy oak club, and strode out into the street.

"Ah, you foolish beast!" shouted the blacksmith, stripping the lion's skin from the trembling animal's back and raining hearty blows across his shoulders. "Your coat might deceive the eye of a stranger, but your ridiculous bray reveals the simple donkey you truly are!"
moral: Fine clothes and grand pretenses can never disguise an empty mind; speech betrays the fool.
